patient_summary:
Hi there! I wanted to explain what's happening with your legs and what you need to do. 

You had some tests done to check how well your blood is flowing in your legs. The tests showed that your blood flow is normal in both legs. This means there's no problem with the blood vessels in your legs.

For your right leg, the tests showed that your blood pressure is normal and your leg pulses look good. For your left leg, the tests also showed normal blood pressure and pulses, but there's a small change in how the blood flows in one part of your leg.

You don't need any medicines right now. The doctors just want to keep an eye on your legs to make sure everything stays normal. 

You should take good care of your legs by:
- Wearing comfortable shoes that fit well
- Not putting anything on your legs that might irritate them
- Keeping your legs moving to help the blood flow better

If you notice any changes in your legs, like pain, swelling, or changes in the color, you should tell your doctor right away. They can check you again and make sure everything is okay.

Remember, you're doing great! Just keep taking good care of your legs.
caregiver_checklist: Check the patient's blood pressure twice a day.
Watch for any signs of leg pain or swelling.
Call the healthcare provider if the patient experiences severe leg pain.
Schedule a follow-up appointment in 6 months.
Check the patient's ankle brachial index every 3 months.
Watch for any changes in the patient's leg color or temperature.
Call the healthcare provider if the patient's ankle brachial index drops below 0.90.
Schedule a repeat arterial imaging in 6 months.
Watch for any signs of infection or wound healing issues.
Call the healthcare provider if the patient has any new or worsening symptoms.
